prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a hit while turning left in League City, Texas, and has whiplash. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1226; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my full name on a recording, but you can use the claim number and the policy holder details you already have.

Q: That works. Can you tell me where the accident happened?

A: It was at an intersection in League City, Texas, on a weekday afternoon. I was turning left onto a side street.

Q: What were you doing right before the collision?

A: I had my turn signal on and was waiting for a gap in oncoming traffic. When it looked clear, I started the turn.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before impact?

A: Not clearly. I saw a set of headlights, but I assumed there was more room than there was. It came through the intersection fast and hit the rear passenger side of my car.

Q: How fast would you estimate you were moving when you started the turn?

A: Maybe ten or fifteen miles an hour. I was almost stopped.

Q: Did you feel any injury at the scene?

A: My neck jerked forward and then back. I felt stiff right away, but I thought it would pass.

Q: Have you sought medical treatment since the accident?

A: Yes, I went to urgent care the next day and was told I have whiplash. I've been doing physical therapy twice a week since then. The neck pain and headaches are still there, and turning my head to check mirrors is hard.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your account?

A: Only that I believe I had the right of way to complete the turn when the vehicle reached me. I'm willing to provide the medical records.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.
